generations.name: Original Defender (90/110)
generations.note: The coil-sprung 90 and 110 became 'Defender' in 1990. Tdi, Td5 and Ford-sourced Puma diesels followed; air conditioning stayed optional for an embarrassingly long time. Production ended in January 2016.

generations.name: New Defender
generations.note: A unibody aluminium platform, independent suspension and air springs — nothing shared with the old car but the name and the silhouette, deliberately. 90, 110 and stretched 130 bodies, up to a supercharged V8.

models.intro: Seventy years of farm, army and expedition service made the original Defender a British institution — and about as comfortable as one. The 2020 replacement kept the name and the look, replaced the ladder frame and live axles with a monocoque, and sold in numbers the original never approached.
models.name: Defender

generations.name: Range Rover Classic
generations.note: Started with a 3.5-litre Rover V8, coil springs when rivals rode on leaves, and a two-door body. It invented the luxury SUV by accident — it was designed as a working estate car.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: BMW-developed, launched with BMW engines, then Jaguar V8s including a supercharged flagship. The generation that completed the move from farm gate to valet stand.

generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.note: Seven seats for the first time in the standard car, twin-turbo BMW V8 power, plug-in hybrids and an interior stripped of nearly every button. The SV is the hand-finished flagship.

models.intro: The original luxury SUV, from 1970: coil springs, a V8, and a design so right that one sat in the Louvre. Every generation since has traded a little more mud-plugging honesty for a lot more polish, and the fifth is now a full-scale limousine that can still wade nearly a metre of water.
models.name: Range Rover

generations.name: Discovery Series I
generations.note: Launched to fight the Japanese SUVs flooding Europe: 200 Tdi diesel or Rover V8, a stepped roof with 'alpine lights' and an interior designed with Terence Conran's studio.

generations.name: Discovery 3 / LR3
generations.note: A clean-sheet design: independent air suspension, seven proper seats and Terrain Response, which made off-road settings a single dial. Heavy, complex and brilliant.

generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.note: Aluminium construction shed serious weight, and the styling split the faithful down the middle — offset rear plate and all. Still seats seven adults and still the tow-and-family pick of the range.

models.intro: The middle child done right: seven seats, real off-road hardware and a stepped roof you can spot a mile away. The Discovery has always been the Land Rover for families who actually leave tarmac, even if the fifth generation dresses like it doesn't.
models.name: Discovery
